papers.title: A note, folded very small
lines: Dear cousin, our guest is well, and eats like a farmer. He asks the hour of the tide twice a day, as if he did not know it was a marsh.
If we should be taken, there is a tin buried at the water's edge, where we used to fish for eels. Tell nobody but the heron.
Burn this, if you can bear to.

trail.clue: A tin buried where the Fens meet the water, near the old eel fishing.

papers.title: A page torn from a prayer book
lines: Brother, the winter was long and the fish were few. I have talked to the ducks, and they have no opinions.
When you come across the water, leave what you can spare in the hollow by the three stones, and take what you need.
I am well. I am, if anything, too well. It is dreadfully peaceful.

trail.clue: A hollow by three stones, on dry ground near the lake at Keswick.

papers.title: A tally on a scrap of paper
lines: Eight kegs, four bales of tobacco, and one cask of something I did not ask about.
The gauger was at the Bloody Bridge again, so we went round by the Hare's Gap.
Third stone from the wall, as before. Do not write this down. (I have written this down.)

trail.clue: The third stone from a wall, somewhere in the Mournes.
